content: Topical gentamicin is a medication applied directly to the skin, typically in the form of a cream or ointment. It is used to treat bacterial skin infections. Below is detailed information about its usage, side effects, precautions, and other important considerations. How to Use: Apply the cream or ointment directly to the affected area of the skin as prescribed by your healthcare provider. If you are treating impetigo, remove any crusts from the infected area before applying the medication. This ensures the antibiotic can effectively reach the infection site. Do not apply this medication to the eyes or any other unintended areas. Common Side Effects: Redness of the skin. Itching of the skin. Irritation at the application site. If any of these side effects persist or worsen, inform your healthcare provider promptly. There may be additional side effects not listed here, so contact your healthcare provider if you suspect any adverse reactions. Serious Side Effects: Although rare, serious allergic reactions can occur. Stop using topical gentamicin immediately and seek medical attention if you experience: Difficulty breathing or wheezing. Rapid heartbeat. Fever or a general feeling of being unwell. Swollen lymph nodes. Swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat. Difficulty swallowing or a sensation of throat tightness. Skin rash, hives, or pale red bumps on the skin. Nausea or vomiting. Dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting. Stomach cramps or joint pain. Additionally, using topical gentamicin may lead to secondary infections caused by other microorganisms, such as fungi. Precautions: Do not use topical gentamicin if you are allergic to gentamicin or any of the ingredients in the product. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients. This medication should only be used if prescribed by a healthcare provider. Do not share it with others, even if they have similar symptoms, as it may harm them. Keep this medication out of the reach of children. Inform your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions and any medications, supplements, or herbal products you are currently using. This will help them determine if topical gentamicin is appropriate for you. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known whether topical gentamicin can harm an unborn baby or affect pregnancy. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is also unknown if topical gentamicin passes into breast milk. Discuss with your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: There are no known interactions between topical gentamicin and foods, drinks, or other medications. However, it is unclear if alcohol consumption affects the medication. Overdose: If you or someone else accidentally uses too much topical gentamicin, seek immediate medical attention. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply double or extra doses. It is crucial to complete the full course of treatment as prescribed, even if symptoms improve or disappear. This reduces the risk of developing antibiotic-resistant infections. Additional Notes: This medication is for external use only and should not be ingested or applied to unintended areas. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions and consult them if you have any questions or concerns about using topical gentamicin.
